sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A publishers section that keeps itself current
sections.para: A publishers page written once falls behind a site that changes daily. So the newsroom has sections, the first for publishers: five pieces to start with, the latest, features with when they shipped, and every relevant article placed by rule, each saying why. Building it exposed loose classification, fixed as rules with reasons.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: One audience's view, placed by rule, explained
sections.para: A section is the newsroom as one audience reads it: start here, latest, features and every relevant article. Articles are placed by rule as they are published and features appear as they ship, each placement saying why. A features register records what the site can do. Publishers come first; other audiences can follow.

sections.label: Where do I send a publisher?
sections.line: The publishers page cannot keep up
sections.para: Publishers ask where to start. The publishers page is a good distillation, but written once, and the site changes most days. The folded reading views, which let a returning reader see only unread sections, shipped on 17 October and no publisher page mentioned them. The page needs to keep up.

sections.label: What a section is
sections.line: Start here, latest, features, streams, and how
sections.para: Between the five desks and the personas sits a section: one audience's view in one place, linked at the top of every page. It has five pieces chosen by the editor, the latest pieces marked new for a week, features with dates and status, four streams of placed articles, and a note on how it stays current.

sections.label: How it keeps itself current
sections.line: Rules over existing data, plus a features register
sections.para: Only the five starting pieces are chosen by hand. Streams are JSON rules over each article's desk and controlled subjects, tried in order. A features register records each feature's purpose, ship date, status and audience, added in the release that ships it. New articles and features appear in the section the day they arrive.

sections.label: What building it showed
sections.para: The first run placed 79 articles, 69 after fixes. History talks were filed as journalism because that subject absorbs history; the agent-readable web was broad enough to catch dark mode; replies went elsewhere first. Each fix is a rule with its reason, the same lesson as search: better taxonomy, less curation.

sections.label: Next sections
sections.line: Security leads, builders and investors next
sections.para: Publishers came first because they are who I most often need to point somewhere. Security leads, builders and investors can each get a section from one more rules file and five starting pieces, and each has a JSON twin an agent can read on someone's behalf.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Hand-picked start, loose tags, one section
sections.para: The start-here list is mine and will go stale unless changed. Placement is only as good as the classification, with three exclusions and two exceptions today. Some features lack a confirmed ship date. Only one section exists, and the imported publishers page is unchanged.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: The section, its rules, data and code
sections.para: From a voice memo on 18 October 2026. The section page, its rules and JSON twin, the features register, the build script admin/build/sections.py and articles/find.json, with related articles on reading views, search as navigation, reviews and the meter.
